# Advanced optimal control

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Self-study**: not taught at the workshop, but complete and ready to use on your own.
:::

Optimal control asks for a time-dependent intervention rather than a single
parameter value. The control is itself a function, so discretizing time and
discretizing a control are modeling choices. This appendix uses `InfiniteOpt`
to state the continuous-time problem and lets its collocation transcription
produce a finite nonlinear program solved by Ipopt.

## Learning goals

By the end of this appendix you should be able to:

- distinguish a continuous-time, function-valued control from the
  finite-dimensional intervention in Chapter 11;
- formulate an ODE-constrained problem with `InfiniteOpt` 0.6;
- inspect the collocated trajectory and check structural identities; and
- explain why the historical nonlinear SDDP example is not a valid current
  SDDP model.

## Model assumptions and classification

We use normalized population fractions, so `S + I` is a fraction and
`C` is cumulative infection incidence divided by `N`. The model is
deterministic, continuous in time and state, population-level, and
ODE-constrained. The control `u(t)` is measurable and bounded between zero and
`u_max`; it reduces transmission by the factor `1 - u(t)`.

The baseline rates remain `β = 0.05`, `c = 10.0`, and `γ = 0.25`, so the
effective transmission rate is `βc = 0.5`. We use
`S(0) = 0.99`, `I(0) = 0.01`, and `C(0) = 0`. The finite horizon is
`t_f = 20`, `u_max = 0.5`, and the intervention budget is
`B = 2.0`. These horizon and budget values are intentionally smaller than a
production policy study.

## Equations

The controlled dynamics are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot S(t) &= -(1-u(t))\beta c\,S(t)I(t),\\
\dot I(t) &= (1-u(t))\beta c\,S(t)I(t)-\gamma I(t),\\
\dot C(t) &= (1-u(t))\beta c\,S(t)I(t).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$ {#eq-a08-controlled-sir}

We minimize final cumulative cases plus a small quadratic regularizer:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underset{S,I,C,u}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad
& C(t_f) + 10^{-3}\int_0^{t_f}u(t)^2\,\mathrm dt\\
\text{subject to}\quad
& 0\le u(t)\le u_{\max},\qquad
\int_0^{t_f}u(t)\,\mathrm dt\le B,
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$ {#eq-a08-objective}

with the initial conditions above. `deriv(S, t)` in the code is
`\dot S(t)`, `integral(u, t)` is the budget measure, and `S(tf)` is a
restricted value of the infinite variable at the terminal time.

This is not the same problem class as the core Chapter 11 example, which
optimizes a finite set of intervention parameters around an ODE simulation.
Here `u` is declared as `Infinite(t)` and is represented numerically by
orthogonal collocation supports.

## Julia implementation

### InfiniteOpt formulation

The following is a complete, current `InfiniteOpt` 0.6 path. The
`OrthogonalCollocation(2)` derivative method supplies a transcription for the
ODE constraints. `constant_over_collocation` prevents the piecewise control
from acquiring extra, unconstrained values at collocation points.

```{julia}
using CairoMakie
using InfiniteOpt
using Ipopt

const a08_tf = 20.0
const a08_beta_c = 0.05 * 10.0
const a08_gamma = 0.25
const a08_umax = 0.5
const a08_budget = 2.0

model = InfiniteModel(Ipopt.Optimizer)
set_optimizer_attribute(model, "print_level", 0)
set_optimizer_attribute(model, "max_iter", 1000)
set_optimizer_attribute(model, "tol", 1e-7)

@infinite_parameter(
    model,
    t in [0.0, a08_tf],
    num_supports = 21,
    derivative_method = OrthogonalCollocation(2),
)

@variable(model, S >= 0, Infinite(t), start = 0.99)
@variable(model, I >= 0, Infinite(t), start = 0.01)
@variable(model, C >= 0, Infinite(t), start = 0.0)
@variable(model, 0 <= u <= a08_umax, Infinite(t), start = 0.0)

@constraint(model, S(0.0) == 0.99)
@constraint(model, I(0.0) == 0.01)
@constraint(model, C(0.0) == 0.0)
@constraint(model, deriv(S, t) == -(1 - u) * a08_beta_c * S * I)
@constraint(model, deriv(I, t) == (1 - u) * a08_beta_c * S * I - a08_gamma * I)
@constraint(model, deriv(C, t) == (1 - u) * a08_beta_c * S * I)
@constraint(model, integral(u, t) <= a08_budget)
@objective(model, Min, C(a08_tf) + 1e-3 * integral(u^2, t))

constant_over_collocation(u, t)
optimize!(model)
```

The solution query uses the same support values for all four time-dependent
variables, which makes the plotted trajectories directly comparable.

```{julia}
solver_status = termination_status(model)
objective = objective_value(model)
time_supports = supports(t)
S_values = value.(S)
I_values = value.(I)
C_values = value.(C)
u_values = value.(u)
(; solver_status, objective, number_of_supports = length(time_supports))
```

### Plotting the policy and trajectory

```{julia}
#| label: fig-a08-infiniteopt
#| fig-cap: "InfiniteOpt's collocated epidemic trajectory and the optimized continuous-time intervention."
fig = Figure(size = (900, 400))
ax1 = Axis(
    fig[1, 1],
    xlabel = "Time",
    ylabel = "Population fraction",
)
lines!(ax1, time_supports, S_values; color = :steelblue, linewidth = 3, label = "S")
lines!(ax1, time_supports, I_values; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 3, label = "I")
lines!(ax1, time_supports, C_values; color = :seagreen, linewidth = 3, label = "C")
axislegend(ax1; position = :lt)

ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel = "Time", ylabel = "Intervention u(t)")
stairs!(ax2, time_supports, u_values; color = :darkorange, linewidth = 3)
hlines!(ax2, [a08_umax]; color = :gray, linestyle = :dash, label = "u_max")
axislegend(ax2; position = :rb)
fig
```

## Validation

Two identities are useful checks for this formulation. Since `C` and `S`
have opposite incidence derivatives,
`C(t) = S(0) - S(t)` should hold. Also, the collocated policy must remain
within its declared bounds. These checks validate the transcription output;
they do not prove global optimality of a nonconvex nonlinear program.

```{julia}
incidence_identity_error = maximum(abs.(0.99 .- S_values .- C_values))
control_bound_violation = maximum(max.(0.0, u_values .- a08_umax))
nonnegative_state_violation = minimum(vcat(S_values, I_values, C_values))
(;
    incidence_identity_error,
    control_bound_violation,
    nonnegative_state_violation,
    solver_status,
)
```

The first two values should be at floating-point or solver tolerance. The
third should be nonnegative. Refining `num_supports` is the natural numerical
convergence check: repeat the model with 41 supports and compare the objective
and the policy at common times.

## Interpretation and limitations

`InfiniteOpt` separates the mathematical infinite-dimensional problem from its
transcription. The result is a policy defined over the time domain, rather
than one value per hand-chosen daily interval. Collocation does not remove
discretization error, and Ipopt reports a local solution for this nonlinear
problem. The budget, bounds, and objective are stylized; real interventions
have delays, costs, compliance, observation feedback, and integer decisions.

The old `../sir-julia/tutorials/sddp/sddp.jmd` example is intentionally not copied
as runnable code here. It places SIR updates containing exponentials and
products of state and control variables inside `SDDP.LinearPolicyGraph` using
`@NLconstraint`. Current SDDP.jl documents policy graphs for multistage
linear, mixed-integer linear, and supported quadratic formulations; arbitrary
nonlinear epidemic dynamics are outside that supported class. Presenting that
old script as current would be misleading. A valid SDDP treatment would first
construct a linear or mixed-integer approximation with an explicit error
analysis, or use a different nonlinear stochastic-control method. See the
[current SDDP manual](https://sddp.dev/stable/) and
[@dowson2021] for the supported decomposition setting.

For the continuous formulation used here, consult the
[InfiniteOpt quick-start guide](https://infiniteopt.github.io/InfiniteOpt.jl/stable/tutorials/quick_start/)
and the package's [official documentation](https://infiniteopt.github.io/InfiniteOpt.jl/stable/).
The one-lockdown structural result discussed by Britton and Leskelä
[@britton2022] is useful context, but it is not used as a fabricated
closed-form validation of this collocated solve.

## Exercises

### Exercise 1 {#a08-ex1}

Repeat the optimization with 21 and 41 time supports. Interpolate both
policies onto a common grid and compare their objectives, final cumulative
cases, and maximum pointwise policy difference. Explain which discrepancy is
transcription error and which could be a different local optimum.

### Exercise 2 {#a08-ex2}

Design a supported SDDP approximation rather than reusing the historical
nonlinear script: use a finite-horizon linear policy graph for a linear
inventory-like intervention budget with exogenous scenario costs. Document
the approximation and its relation to the SIR objective, then explain which
epidemic nonlinearities have been discarded. Do not claim that an SDDP
solution is an exact solution of @eq-a08-controlled-sir.
